events.summary: Officials announced a national tax week beginning July 6, followed by year-round public tax education.
Kalubowila Hospital plans to open a cath lab, angiography unit and lithotripsy unit on June 30.
Jaffna Teaching Hospital's cath lab was inaugurated on June 27.
Government asset sales generated Rs. 4,040.9 million over 16 months.
Officials asked owners of rooftop solar systems above 300 units to switch them off for three days.
Seven battery storage systems arrived in Colombo for installation near substations.
Internal auditors opened stores and found expired food and relief supplies intended for displaced people.
The minister outlined plans to recruit 13,600 nurses by 2030.
Health Ministry planned four new cath labs for Jaffna, Kalubowila and Colombo hospitals.
National drug-operation headquarters and media centre scheduled to open in Colombo.
Aswesuma payments for 425,000 vulnerable-category beneficiaries stopped in June.
Central Province decided to invite bids again and re-auction several vehicles.
One luxury vehicle was valued at approximately 40 million rupees.
Nationwide updates to Aswesuma beneficiary information were underway.
President directed Treasury officials to allocate funds for Yala-season paddy purchases.
Sri Lanka officially received ten US-donated TH-57 Sea Ranger helicopters.
Cabinet approved a new computer network across all Examinations Department branches.
Cabinet approved electrifying three high-density railway corridors from Maradana.
A Salary and Pension Commission was established by presidential action and gazette.
Health Ministry launched guidelines for healthy, safe, affordable food in school canteens.
India-supported hybrid solar, wind and battery systems are under construction on three Jaffna islands.
State agencies prepared water, power, health, transport and security services for Poson pilgrims.
A CT scanner worth over LKR 200 million was installed at Kalutara Teaching Hospital.
ADB-supported CT scanners worth about LKR 640 million were supplied to four hospitals; installation continues.
The Ministry is preparing to purchase scanners for five hospitals at an estimated LKR 950 million.
Government vehicle and asset sales generated revenue over 16 months.
Foton prepared to send all 104 tendered Metro buses to Sri Lanka.
Rail services between Nanu Oya and Badulla are scheduled to resume.
The Postal Department prepared permanent appointments for 192 acting sub-postmasters.
Government launched the 2026–2030 National Export Development Plan.
Cabinet approved the plan as Sri Lanka’s official export-development strategy.
Cabinet approved drafting a national plan to reduce human-elephant conflict.
Restoration work began on the Kalawewa reservoir spillway.
The restoration investment was estimated at more than Rs. 75 million.
Ranick International received the spillway restoration construction contract.
Cabinet approved funds to restore 90 additional religious sites damaged by Cyclone Ditwah.
Online registration became available for expressway electronic toll collection.
Colombo District Dengue Committee launched a week of intensive dengue control activities.
President directed officials to complete work on a proposed national education policy framework within one month.
President instructed officials to prepare plans for water, agriculture, food security and continuous electricity amid El Niño risks.
National Export Development Plan scheduled for official launch on June 16 in Colombo.
Wetahirkanda elephant corridor restoration and protection measures are being implemented.
Officials agreed to prepare a fertilizer import and distribution plan for Maha season.
Domestic donations for Cyclone Ditwah relief were recorded in Treasury accounts by May 31.
Foreign assistance for Cyclone Ditwah relief was received through the Central Bank and state banks by May 31.
Online registration began for government institutions using officials’ concessionary railway season tickets.
The 2026 budget allocated funding for a women’s entrepreneurship empowerment programme.
Cabinet approved the proposed women’s entrepreneurship empowerment programme implementation plan.
The three-day national dengue mosquito-control programme began across 14 districts.
Government launched the national education management system’s human-resources module and e-Thaksalawa learning pilot.
A local company demonstrated an agricultural drone for seeding and fertiliser application at a workshop.
The government raised the fertiliser subsidy to LKR 30,000 per hectare; LKR 10.947 billion has been spent.
Government spent LKR 1.859 billion to purchase an additional 15,000 tonnes of urea fertiliser.
A four-year programme to address gaps at basic hospitals is being implemented.
The Agricultural and Agrarian Insurance Board planned insurance coverage for qualifying coffee cultivation.
Tripartite cooperation agreement signed for a 150 MW wind farm and integrated battery storage.
People’s Bank held a financial literacy workshop for 71 entrepreneurs.
District officials were asked to establish a system for faster fertiliser testing.
Health Ministry has spent over Rs. 857 million on the ward complex.
Health Ministry expects to spend over Rs. 2.9 billion on the full project.
Five-storey maternal and surgical ward complex was completed.
Ten US-donated helicopters arrived and are being assembled at Ratmalana Air Force Base.
Rs. 1 billion allocated this year for cooperative rice drying, storage and related facility improvements.
A Rs. 500 million project to provide rice-drying machines to cooperatives is being implemented.
A Rs. 100 million project to buy production and packaging machinery for producer cooperatives is being implemented.
Central Bank scheduled the next digital-payments promotion event in Trincomalee for June 5 and 6.
Finance Committee decided to establish weekly reporting on rice used for food, feed and industry.
Health Ministry invited applications to recruit 3,000 nursing trainees for 2026.
Airport bus service between Bandaranaike International Airport and Makumbura resumed.
